# XDL — Extended Data Language (Rust)

> A Rust reimplementation of GNU Data Language (GDL) / IDL: lexer, parser,
> tree-walking interpreter, 754-entry standard library, 2D/3D plotting, GPU
> acceleration, a language server, and a VS Code extension. Cargo workspace of 18
> crates (17 listed in `members`, plus `xdl-matlab` auto-included as a path dep),
> and one crate outside it.
> Docs: https://turingworks.github.io/xdl · Repo: https://github.com/turingworks/xdl

## Running XDL

```bash
cargo build --release -p xdl-cli
./target/release/xdl script.xdl            # run a file
./target/release/xdl -e 'print, findgen(5)'  # one-liner
./target/release/xdl -i                    # REPL
./target/release/xdl parse script.xdl      # dump the AST
./target/release/xdl test tests            # run the .xdl suite in a directory
```

Flags: `-e/--execute <CMD>`, `-i/--interactive`, `-v/--verbose`, `-q/--quiet`.

## Language quick reference

Comments start with `;`. Names are **case-insensitive**. Arrays are **0-based**.

```idl
; variables and arrays
x = 42
arr = [1, 2, 3]
a = findgen(10)          ; 0.0 .. 9.0
m = fltarr(3, 4)         ; 3x4 float array

; procedures are statement-style, functions are call-style
print, "value =", x
y = sin(a)

; keywords: named, optional, order-independent; /KEY sets it to 1
plot, x, y, title="Demo", /ylog

; conditionals
if x gt 5 then begin
  print, "big"
end else begin
  print, "small"
end
endif

; loops
for i = 0, 9 do begin
  print, i
endfor

while count gt 0 do begin
  count = count - 1
end
endwhile

repeat begin
  n = n + 1
end until n ge 10

foreach element, arr do begin
  print, element
endfor

case value of
  1: print, "one"
  2: print, "two"
  else: print, "other"
endcase

; user-defined routines
pro my_proc, a, b
  print, a + b
end

function my_func, a
  return, a * 2
end
```

Operators: `+ - * / ^ mod`, comparison `eq ne lt le gt ge`, logical
`and or not xor`, `#` matrix multiply, `->` method call, `*` pointer
dereference.

System variables are `!`-prefixed: `!PI`, `!VALUES.F_NAN`, `!P`, `!X`, `!Y`, `!D`.

## Built-in function categories (754 dispatch entries)

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Math | `SIN COS TAN EXP ALOG SQRT ABS FFT` |
| Special math | `ERF ERFC GAMMA LNGAMMA FACTORIAL BESELJ BESELY BESELI BESELK` |
| Type conversion | `BYTE INT UINT LONG ULONG LONG64 ULONG64 FLOAT DOUBLE FIX COMPLEX` |
| Array creation | `FINDGEN INDGEN DINDGEN FLTARR DBLARR INTARR MAKE_ARRAY RANDOMU RANDOMN` |
| Array ops | `TRANSPOSE REFORM REVERSE SORT WHERE SHIFT ROTATE REPLICATE UNIQ TOTAL N_ELEMENTS SIZE` |
| Statistics | `MEAN VARIANCE STDDEV MEDIAN MOMENT KURTOSIS SKEWNESS LINFIT POLY_FIT CORRELATE` |
| Interpolation | `INTERPOL SPLINE BILINEAR` |
| Linear algebra | `INVERT DETERM SVDC LUDC LA_EIGENVAL CRAMER` |
| Signal processing | `A_CORRELATE C_CORRELATE CONVOL DIGITAL_FILTER HILBERT SMOOTH` |
| Image processing | `DILATE ERODE SOBEL ROBERTS GAUSSIAN_FILTER HISTOGRAM` |
| Strings | `STRLEN STRPOS STRMID STRJOIN STRSPLIT STRCMP STRTRIM STRUPCASE STRLOWCASE` |
| File I/O | `OPENR OPENW OPENU READF WRITEF READU WRITEU CLOSE FILE_TEST FILE_INFO FILE_SEARCH` |
| Scientific I/O | FITS, HDF5, NetCDF readers/writers (`xdl-stdlib/src/scientific_io.rs`) |
| Time | `SYSTIME JULDAY CALDAT TIC TOC` |
| MATLAB compat | `LINSPACE LOGSPACE REPMAT SQUEEZE NDGRID INTERP1 MESHGRID` |
| DataFrames (feature `dataframes`) | `DF_READ_CSV DF_FILTER DF_GROUPBY DF_JOIN DF_SORT` |
| ML (feature `ml`) | `ML_KMEANS_* ML_LINEAR_* ML_PCA_* ML_ACCURACY ML_MSE ML_R2_SCORE` |
| Python (feature `python`) | `PYTHON_IMPORT PYTHON_CALL PYTHON_CALL_KW` |

Graphics **procedures** (statement-style, ~50): `PLOT OPLOT PLOTS XYOUTS AXIS
CONTOUR SURFACE SHADE_SURF PLOT3D ISOSURFACE ISOCONTOUR TV TVSCL WINDOW WSET
WDELETE LOADCT SET_PLOT_BACKEND`.

Functions and procedures are **separate registries**
(`call_function*` vs `call_procedure*` in `xdl-stdlib/src/lib.rs`).

## Cargo features

| Feature | Enables |
|---|---|
| `python` | PyO3 bridge to a system Python |
| `rustpython` | embedded pure-Rust Python |
| `dataframes` | Polars-backed `DF_*` functions (**default**) |
| `ml` | Linfa-backed `ML_*` functions (**default**, via `datascience`) |

Additional gates: `stats` (statrs), `gis` (proj/geo), `scientific-io` (netcdf +
hdf5), `image-io`. `xdl-stdlib`'s default is `["dataframes", "datascience"]`, so
`dataframes`, `stats`, and `ml` are **on by default**; `python`, `rustpython`,
`gis`, and `scientific-io` are not, and the last three need system libraries —
`--all-features` fails without them, for reasons unrelated to your change.

A function behind a disabled feature must
still be nameable and must return an error saying which feature is missing —
never "unknown function".

## Crate map

```
xdl-core         XdlValue, XdlArray, Dimension, XdlError/XdlResult
xdl-parser       lexer.rs → ast.rs → parser.rs
xdl-interpreter  evaluator.rs (tree-walk), context.rs, methods.rs
xdl-runtime      memory + GC scaffolding
xdl-stdlib       lib.rs = THE DISPATCH (754 arms) + 30 implementation modules
xdl-cli          the `xdl` binary: file runner, REPL, parse, test
xdl-ffi          C embedding surface + GSL / HDF5 / NetCDF wrappers
xdl-gui          egui plot + image windows
xdl-charts       ECharts HTML generation
xdl-chart-viewer Tauri viewer app (own tauri.conf.json)
xdl-viz3d        wgpu 3D engine   (+ -web HTTP server, + -threejs templates)
xdl-amp          13 GPU/SIMD backends behind dispatch.rs
xdl-dataframe    Polars integration
xdl-database     SQL access from XDL
xdl-lsp          language server: completion, hover, goto, symbols, diagnostics
vscode-xdl       TextMate grammar + extension that launches xdl-lsp

xdl-matlab       .m → XDL transpiler. Not in [workspace] members, but a path
                 dependency of xdl-cli and xdl-gui, so Cargo auto-includes it and
                 --workspace covers its lib (not its tests: cargo test -p xdl-matlab).

Outside the workspace — nothing depends on it, nothing compiles it:
xdl-desktop-viewer   Tauri; check with --manifest-path after a core-type change
```

## Adding a built-in — the six places

1. `xdl-stdlib/src/<module>.rs` — `fn f(args: &[XdlValue]) -> XdlResult<XdlValue>`
2. `xdl-stdlib/src/lib.rs` — `"NAME" => module::f(args),` **fully uppercase**
   (dispatch runs `name.to_uppercase()`; a lowercase arm is dead code)
3. `xdl-lsp/src/symbols.rs` — `builtin_functions` entry (name, doc, return, signature)
4. `vscode-xdl/syntaxes/xdl.tmLanguage.json` — the builtin-name pattern
5. `docs/` — reference entry
6. `tests/*.xdl` — a script that calls it

Only step 2 is checked by the compiler, and only for type errors.
`scripts/check-builtin-parity.sh` compares steps 2 and 3.

## Build, test, lint

```bash
cargo check --workspace                    # what the edit hook runs (18 crates)
cargo check --manifest-path xdl-desktop-viewer/Cargo.toml  # not compiled by --workspace
cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast      # ALWAYS --no-fail-fast
cargo test -p xdl-matlab                   # its tests are not in --workspace --all-targets
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all
cargo bench                                # criterion
scripts/check-builtin-parity.sh            # stdlib ↔ LSP name drift
scripts/check-version-sync.sh              # Cargo.toml ↔ tauri.conf.json ↔ package.json
scripts/check-docs-links.sh                # relative links in docs/
```

## Agent guidance

- `CLAUDE.md` — entry point: answer style, quick reference, cross-cutting checklist
- `AGENTS.md` — authoritative: product matrix, change-surface cookbook, functional
  style, IDL semantics, performance, numerical honesty, verification, test isolation
- `SOUL.md` — what XDL is for and why compatibility is not negotiable
- `.claude/skills/add-builtin/SKILL.md` — the ordered walk-through for a new built-in
